title: Mushroom Lasagne
subtitle: Mixed mushroom lasagne with cream, thyme, and Parmesan
excerpt: Mushroom lasagne layers a rich mixture of mixed mushrooms cooked with garlic, thyme, and a splash of cream with béchamel and pasta sheets. The mushrooms provide a deep savoury flavour that makes the dish satisfying without meat. Dried porcini mixed into the fresh mushrooms add intensity.
sourceNotes: Mushroom lasagne using a combination of fresh and dried mushrooms is a British and Italian vegetarian adaptation. The use of dried porcini for depth is standard in Italian mushroom preparations.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool completely and freeze for up to 3 months.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to 24 hours ahead and refrigerate unbaked.

content.text: Mushroom lasagne uses a mix of fresh mushrooms cooked until their moisture has evaporated and they are deeply concentrated and golden, combined with rehydrated dried porcini for a rich, earthy flavour. The mushroom filling is creamy and intense; the béchamel lightens the layers. The dish is for autumn, when mushroom flavour is at its best.

items.prepNote: soaked in 200 ml boiling water for 20 minutes, drained and chopped (reserve soaking liquid)

content.text: Soak {{dried-porcini}} of dried porcini in 200 ml of boiling water for 20 minutes. Drain (reserving the soaking liquid), squeeze dry, and chop. Strain the soaking liquid through a fine sieve to remove any grit.

Heat {{olive-oil}} of olive oil in a large frying pan over a high heat. Add the {{mushrooms-chestnut}} of sliced fresh mushrooms in batches, cooking without stirring for 3 to 4 minutes until golden. Stir, add the porcini and {{garlic}} of garlic, and cook for 2 more minutes. Add the {{thyme}} sprigs and the strained porcini soaking liquid. Cook until the liquid has evaporated. Remove the thyme. Stir in {{double-cream}} of cream and cook for 2 minutes until the filling is glossy. Season with {{salt-table}} of salt and {{black-pepper}} of pepper.

Heat the oven to 190°C (fan 170°C / gas mark 5). Melt {{unsalted-butter}} of butter, add {{plain-flour}} of flour, stir 2 minutes. Whisk in {{whole-milk}} of warm milk gradually. Stir over medium heat until thick, 5 to 6 minutes. Season with {{nutmeg}} of nutmeg and a pinch of salt.

Spread a thin layer of béchamel in the base of the baking tin. Add a layer of {{lasagne-sheets}} pasta sheets. Spread half the mushroom filling and a quarter of the remaining béchamel. Scatter some {{parmesan}} of Parmesan. Repeat: pasta, remaining mushroom filling, béchamel, Parmesan. Finish with pasta, béchamel, and Parmesan. Cover with foil and bake 30 minutes. Remove foil and bake 20 more minutes until golden. Rest 10 minutes.

items.cause: The mushrooms were crowded in the pan and steamed rather than sautéed.
items.fix: Cook the mushrooms in batches over high heat. A crowded pan traps steam and prevents the browning that concentrates flavour and drives off moisture.

items.cause: The soaking liquid was discarded or not concentrated enough.
items.fix: Add the strained porcini soaking liquid to the pan and cook until it has evaporated. It is the most intensely flavoured part of the dried mushroom.

content.text: Mushroom lasagne is at home in autumn, when the first cold weather arrives and the appetite moves toward richer, longer-cooked food. It is better than the aubergine version in terms of depth of flavour; the combination of fresh chestnut mushrooms and dried porcini produces a savouriness that sits close to a good meat ragù. It works as a dinner-party main course for vegetarians because nothing about it reads as compromise.
